title: Prompts and messages
lead: Why does one itinerary fit your needs while another reads like a list of attractions?

sections.title: State the requirements
sections.body:
“Plan a trip” and “Two days in Hangzhou with an older family member, short walks, at most two attractions per day” supply different information.
A prompt is content supplied to a model. Explicit tasks, background, constraints, and output requirements make results easier to assess.

sections.title: System: how the service works
sections.body:
A travel assistant might use: “Plan relaxed trips. Ask for missing details and do not invent opening hours.”
APIs supporting the system role let applications provide these ongoing instructions. They guide output without guaranteeing compliance.

sections.title: User: this particular request
sections.body:
“Two days in Hangzhou this weekend, with an older family member and short walks” is the current task, typically supplied in a user message.
Separating application instructions from trip requirements makes both easier to maintain.

sections.title: Assistant: what was said earlier
sections.body:
After receiving an itinerary, a user asks to make day two easier. The model needs the earlier plan to interpret that request.
Assistant messages commonly record earlier model replies. The example combines these roles; supported roles and formats depend on the API.

note: Keep the trip requirements and switch the priority from short walks to local food. Compare the trade-offs, and verify real distances and opening hours.
